==========================================================================
HAZARD 1 -- an unquoted -flag=value.N token is split at the dot
==========================================================================

PowerShell's native-argument parser splits a token that starts with '-',
contains '=', and then contains '.'. dxc then reports an unknown target
environment, which reads exactly like a real DXC limitation.

  unquoted           -fspv-target-env=universal1.5      -> ['-fspv-target-env=universal1', '.5']
  single-quoted      '-fspv-target-env=universal1.5'    -> ['-fspv-target-env=universal1.5']
  unquoted -D        -Dfoo=1.5                          -> ['-Dfoo=1', '.5']
  no leading dash    plain1.5                           -> ['plain1.5']

  and what dxc says when it receives the split form:
    unquoted     : error: unknown SPIR-V target environment 'universal1'
    single-quoted: OpDecorate %foo LinkageAttributes "foo" Export

==========================================================================
HAZARD 2 -- $LASTEXITCODE is STALE after '| Select-Object -First N'
==========================================================================

Select-Object -First N stops the upstream pipeline early, so PowerShell
never reaps the native process and $LASTEXITCODE is left holding a value
that has nothing to do with the compile. The value observed varies (-1
here; 0 in an interactive session where the previous statement was not a
native command). Either way it is not dxc's exit code, and the 0 case
means a failing compile silently reports success.

  fresh shell, piped through Select-Object -First 2    exit=-1
  fresh shell, no early termination                    exit=-2147467259
  fresh shell, no pipeline at all                      exit=-2147467259

  0x80004005 = 2147500037 unsigned = -2147467259 signed. Python's
  returncode reports the unsigned form, PowerShell the signed form;
  they are the same E_FAIL, which is an ordinary diagnosed error and
  NOT a crash.
